title: Pho Bo
subtitle: Vietnamese beef noodle soup with star anise and cinnamon broth
excerpt: Pho bo is Vietnam's national dish -- a long-simmered bone broth fragrant with star anise, cinnamon, and charred ginger. The broth is the heart of the dish. Everything else -- noodles, rare beef, fresh herbs -- is secondary. The charring of the onion and ginger before adding to the broth is the defining technique.
sourceNotes: Pho is thought to have originated in northern Vietnam in the early twentieth century, possibly with French and Chinese influences. The dish spread south after the partition of Vietnam in 1954 and became more elaborate with additional herbs and garnishes. It is now one of the most recognised Vietnamese exports worldwide.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The broth can be made a day ahead and reheated. It improves overnight.

content.text: Pho is a project, not a quick dinner. The broth needs at least 2.5 hours at a low simmer. The payoff is a clear, deeply flavoured broth that tastes like nothing else. The charring of the onion and ginger is not decorative -- it adds a smoky sweetness that defines the dish.

items.prepNote: use beef bones if available -- plus 300g brisket for slicing
beef bone broth or good beef stock
halved and charred directly over a flame or under a grill until blackened
halved and charred under a grill until blackened
use 400g flat rice noodles -- soak in warm water until pliable, then drain
fresh sliced chilli to serve, if available

content.text: Char the onion and ginger halves under a hot grill or directly over a gas flame until blackened all over -- about 5 minutes. This gives the broth its characteristic colour and depth.
Place the beef, charred onion, charred ginger, star anise, cinnamon, and beef stock in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil. Skim off any foam. Reduce to a very low simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 2.5 to 3 hours. The broth should reduce and deepen in colour. Season with fish sauce and salt.
Remove the beef. Slice thinly across the grain. Strain the broth through a fine sieve -- discard the solids.
Cook the noodles according to the packet. Drain and divide between deep bowls.
Lay sliced beef over the noodles. Ladle the boiling broth over the top -- this cooks the beef slightly. Top with spring onion and serve with lime wedges and chilli.

items.symptom: Broth is cloudy and lacks clarity
items.cause: Boiled too hard or foam not skimmed
items.fix: Pho broth should be a gentle, barely-moving simmer. Vigorous boiling clouds the broth. Skim carefully after the first 15 minutes. If it is already cloudy, pass it through a fine sieve lined with a clean cloth.

content.text: Pho is Vietnam's most famous dish. It is eaten for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Northern pho (Hanoi style) is clean and spare. Southern pho (Saigon style) comes with a plate of fresh herbs, bean sprouts, and basil to add at the table. The broth takes hours -- the rest takes minutes.
